summary: Selection sort repeatedly finds the smallest unsorted value and swaps it into place. Insertion sort takes each value and shifts larger values right until it fits.
notes: int temp = items[i]; saves the first value before items[i] is overwritten.
The outer loop of selection sort runs items.length - 1 times. The last value is already in place.
Arrays.toString(items) prints the contents. Printing items alone shows something like [I@1b6d3586.
pitfall: Swapping without temp, items[i] = items[smallest]; items[smallest] = items[i];, copies one value into both spots and loses the other.
